html:
The Entiat are an Interior Salish people of the Entiat River valley in central Washington, where it flows into the Columbia River north of Wenatchee. They speak a dialect of the language shared with the Wenatchi.

They lived by salmon fishing at the river mouths, root digging and hunting in the Cascade foothills. They were not party to any treaty of their own, and in the late 1800s settlers took the valley. Today their descendants are members of the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation. Their neighbours included the Chelan to the north.
